outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are expected from portions of the southern Plains through the Ozarks, Ohio Valley and Middle Atlantic States Wednesday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Slow eastward advance of an upper trough is expected across the Plains states today, while troughing lingers farther west as an upper low persists near the Pacific Northwest. Farther east, fast westerly flow will continue across the Northeast, while upper ridging prevails over the southeast. At the surface, a frontal zone will linger from the mid Atlantic region across the Ohio Valley vicinity, while western fringes of the front shift southeastward across the southern Plains through the end of the period.

sections.title: The southern Plains northeast into the Midwest/Ohio Valley
sections.text: A rather complex convective evolution is expected across this region today, with multiple rounds of storms expected in some areas. Initial severe risks at the start of the period may exist over the mid Mississippi Valley (with ongoing/gradually diminishing storms), and across parts of western Texas (with a second area of ongoing convection). Both of these ongoing convective areas will influence severe weather risk. With the mid Mississippi Valley convection, questions exist regarding details of the airmass recovery across parts of the Missouri/Illinois vicinity. With the Texas storms, speed/location of the storms through mid morning will define the western fringe of the higher severe risk expected to evolve by afternoon. At this time, it appears that Texas storms will move quickly northeastward across north Texas through the morning, central and eastern Oklahoma through midday/early afternoon, and then across the Ozarks through the rest of the afternoon. Severe risk will accompany this convection, with all severe hazards possible locally. sections.title: Upper Ohio Valley east to the mid Atlantic Coast
sections.text: In the wake of remnant/early-morning convection, airmass recovery/destabilization is forecast ahead of a short-wave trough (now centered near southern Lake Michigan) which will cross Lake Erie and reach western Pennsylvania by early afternoon. As this feature -- and a weak/associated surface low -- advances, redevelopment of scattered thunderstorms is forecast to occur, possibly beginning as early as midday, across Pennsylvania, and adjacent parts of West Virginia, Maryland, and northern Virginia. With the airmass forecast to become moderately unstable, storms should quickly intensify -- aided by the persistent belt of strong westerly deep-layer flow across the area. While some tornado risk is expected -- particularly near/ahead of the weak surface low and associated warm front, where backed low-level flow will be present, the greater risks appear to be locally damaging winds, and hail. Some CAM guidance suggests that storms may grow upscale through the afternoon, eventually merging into an at least loosely organized cluster, as it sweeps across eastern portions of the risk area and off the Atlantic coast during the evening. outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are likely from portions of the southern Plains through the Ozarks, and across the Ohio Valley to the north-central Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic States today and tonight.

sections.title: Texas and southern/eastern Oklahoma to Arkansas/Missouri
sections.text: The early-day evolution and probable upscale growth of storms across southwest/western north Texas today will largely regulate the northern fringe of the primary severe risk today. Early today, it seems like that linearly organized strong-to-severe storms will continue to persist and increase/intensify east-northeastward from west Texas into north Texas and southern/eastern Oklahoma through late morning/early this afternoon, reaching parts of Arkansas/southern Missouri later this afternoon into evening. The leading edge of these storms will be capable of damaging winds, particularly as the boundary layer warms this afternoon, along with some QLCS-related tornado risk. On the southern and eastern fringe of this evolving and upscale-expanding convective cluster, more isolated/semi-discrete storms are expected, within what is likely to be a thermodynamic and kinematic environment favorable for supercells, or at least a mixed mode of clusters/possible supercells. Given the possibility of a more cellular storm mode (prior to storms merging with the line), a semi-focused risk for tornadoes appears to exist within a corridor from north-central/northeast Texas and southeast Oklahoma into w

sections.title: Iowa/Illinois/Indiana/Ohio
sections.text: MCS-related convective overturning (reference 12Z Lincoln IL observed sounding) has considerably influenced the region since last evening/overnight, with persistent/regenerative warm-advection-related storms continuing to reinforce an outflow-related effective boundary across far southern portions of Illinois and Indiana early this morning. Short-term global models such as the 06Z NAM/early morning RAP guidance and even recent HRRR runs remain very optimistic, probably too much so, in terms of air mass recovery across the region today, northward to the vicinity of low pressure across Iowa/northwest Illinois and the synoptic boundary location across northern portions of Illinois/Indiana/Ohio. A special 18Z sounding from central Illinois/ILX will help better assess possible air mass recovery through early afternoon. Even with semi-aggressive air mass recovery through the afternoon and the possibility of moderate destabilization by peak heating, overall convergence should tend to remain weak, with most convection-allowing guidance generally only indicative of a relatively isolated risk. sections.title: Upper Ohio Valley/central Appalachians to Mid-Atlantic
sections.text: A convectively enhanced shortwave trough approaching Lake Erie this morning will continue eastward and cross Pennsylvania and the coastal Northeast this afternoon/early evening in conjunction with a belt of strengthening mid-level winds (50-70 kt at 500 mb). As the air mass steadily destabilizes and inhibition erodes by afternoon, scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop and intensify as early as midday across Pennsylvania, and subsequently spread into/across adjacent parts of New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, and northern Virginia. With the air mass likely to become moderately unstable by afternoon, storms will quickly intensify, organizationally aided by the intensifying belt of strong westerly deep-layer flow across the area. Large hail and damaging winds can be expected. Some tornado risk may also exist, particularly across eastern Pennsylvania/New Jersey southward toward the Delmarva vicinity, in relatively close proximity to a surface low and adjacent warm front. sections.title: PA/Mid-Atlantic area this afternoon/evening
sections.text: An embedded mid-upper speed max in the vicinity of Lake Erie will move east-southeastward over PA this afternoon, inducing a weak surface wave along a stalled front from PA into NJ. Deep-layer vertical shear and buoyancy will be favorable for supercells and organized storm clusters capable of producing large hail and damaging winds. Similar to yesterday, a tornado or two will be possible with storms that interact with the baroclinic zone across northern and eastern PA into NJ. The backdoor front and cool marine influence will tend to limit the northeast extent of the surface-based severe threat across NJ/northeastern PA.

sections.title: WV/KY this afternoon
sections.text: Overnight and morning convection has intensified some as of midday, as the low levels warm/destabilize in advance of the convection from central KY to WV. The background environment has sufficient deep-layer west-southwesterly flow/shear and moderate buoyancy to maintain a damaging wind/large hail threat through the afternoon. The orientation of the convective band approaching WV is more favorable to produce damaging winds compared to the more east-west orientation in KY. However, there is still potential for a cluster of storms to move eastward along the more east-west boundary in KY with some damaging wind/hail potential, in addition to locally heavy rainfall.

sections.title: TX to MO through tonight
sections.text: Ongoing convection is becoming more widespread from north TX across eastern OK as of late morning, and storms should continue to expand eastward into northeast TX/AR and northeastward into MO through the afternoon. An increase in storm coverage will be supported by surface heating/mixing weakening the cap to the east and southeast of the ongoing storms, such that additional warm sector development is expected from northeast TX into western AR. There will also be larger-scale support for ascent as an embedded shortwave trough ejects east-northeastward from far west TX over north TX/OK/AR through tonight. Steep midlevel lapse rates and rich low-level moisture are contributing to moderate-strong buoyancy in the warm sector, which will support robust updrafts and downdrafts. Deep-layer vertical shear is in the range supportive of supercells and organized clusters. However, low-level flow/shear is rather disorganized this morning, and only a modest increase in low-level shear is expected this afternoon in areas removed from ongoing convection. outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms will persist from portions of the southern Plains through the Ozarks, and across the Ohio Valley to the north-central Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic States this afternoon into tonight.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Have expanded slight risk area farther east into VA to account for an MCS associated with an MCV crossing the southern Appalachians that might remain capable of producing damaging wind gusts next few hours. Otherwise, only modest adjustments to previous forecast, mainly to trim areas that have been convectively overturned. Despite stabilization due to widespread overturning from eastern KY into southern OH, have left low end slight risk probabilities for the possibility of some recovery in these areas this evening and tonight. ..Dial.. 05/29/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1135 AM CDT Wed May 29 2019/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat is expected to increase across north Texas and southern to central Oklahoma this morning. An isolated tornado threat along with wind damage and hail will be possible as storms move northeastward across the region this morning. A tornado watch may be necessary once uncertainty decreases concerning timing.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The latest radar imagery shows a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms across west-central Texas located just to the west of an axis of moderate to strong instability. The RAP is analyzing MLCAPE in the 2000 to 2500 J/kg range across north Texas with a pocket of 3000+ located in southern Oklahoma. In addition, the RAP is showing a 40 to 50 kt low-level jet over central Texas which is moving north and strengthening. This feature will move northward toward the Red River resulting in a more favorable low-level shear environment for tornadoes. Short-term models develop discrete cells this morning from northwest Texas into southern and central Oklahoma. However, the exact timing is a bit uncertain. Once initiation takes place, supercell development will be likely. An isolated tornado threat, wind damage and hail will be possible. WW issuance will likely be needed across the region.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A cold front has pushed southward across the watch, but elevated storms still have the potential to produce severe hail. A watch extension may be necessary.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Elevated storms continue across portions of WW285 this morning north of a cold front that has moved southward across the southern Plains. Per observations/mesoanalysis a mid-level jet in the vicinity of the ongoing convection is helping to provide forcing for ascent and strengthen deep-layer shear (effective bulk shear of 45-55 knots per mesoanalysis/observed soundings). A moist/buoyant profile noted by 1000-2000+ J/kg of MUCAPE per mesoanalysis is helping to sustain convection across the watch. Storm motion will be to the east/northeast, but continued development is likely across the watch. The threat will eventually move to the east as the mid-level jet/shortwave trough tracks to the northeast, but continued development will occur until it moves out of the area. Additionally, if the vorticity max to the west takes a more southerly/easterly track, strong/severe storm development may continue longer than previously expected. A watch extension may be necessary until 16/17z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A gradual increase in a strong/damaging wind and hail threat may lead to watch issuance later this morning.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A convectively reinforced outflow boundary was located roughly along the OH River at 14Z this morning. Visible satellite imagery and surface observations show gradual destabilization is occurring across much of KY to the south of this boundary, and MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/kg should exist across this region through the morning and into the afternoon. The convection located mainly east-west along the OH River is oriented roughly parallel to the mid-level flow, and it remains unclear how much of a severe threat will evolve from this activity. Of slightly greater concern are the thunderstorms that are beginning to strengthen across western KY and far southern IL in association with a low-amplitude shortwave trough. These thunderstorms will be oriented more perpendicular to the west-southwesterly mid-level flow, and one or more clusters of convection may eventually evolve eastward across KY later this morning into the afternoon. Although mid-level flow is not overly strong, 35-40 kt of effective bulk shear will be enough to organize updrafts, and strong/damaging winds could occur. Any convection that can remain semi-discrete may also pose some hail risk. Depending on convective trends, a watch may be needed at some point later this morning.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Ongoing thunderstorms should continue to strengthen this morning into the afternoon with mainly a large hail and damaging wind threat. Watch issuance is likely soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several thunderstorm clusters ongoing at 1440Z along/ahead of a cold front will likely continue moving east-northward into a favorable environment to support severe hail/wind through the remainder of the morning. MLCAPE of 2000-2500 J/kg and effective bulk shear of generally 40-50 kt will easily support updraft organization. Large hail will be possible with any supercell structures, and damaging winds may occur with the more clustery convection. In addition, a tornado or two will be possible, although the low-level flow is forecast to gradually weaken through much of the daytime hours. Additional storm development is likely through the early afternoon across eastern OK into northwestern AR and southwestern MO, and watch issuance is likely soon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms are expected to intensify in the coming hours along over West Virginia/vicinity ahead of the line storms across southern Ohio and northern Kentucky. Severe hail/wind are the main threats and a watch issuance is possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong mid-level west/southwest flow (upwards of 50 knots) is currently streaming over Ohio Valley into the Northeast per observations/mesoanalysis. A southwest-northeast QLCS has developed in the Ohio Valley and continues to move south/east. On the eastern edge, the orientation of the QLCS is more perpendicular to the west/southwest flow with a warm/moist/unstable airmass downstream. Additionally, discrete storms have started to develop in West Virginia as thermal/terrain circulations help break the cap within the warm sector. Updrafts have struggled to establish ahead of the QLCS, but it is likely discrete cells including some supercells will develop ahead of the QLCS in moderately sheared/buoyant environment (effective bulk shear 35-45 knots/1000-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE). Severe hail/wind are the primary threats associated with the QLCS and discrete storms ahead of the line across much of West Virginia/vicinity. Storms will move eastward across the region during the afternoon and a watch issuance is possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected to develop this afternoon. Large hail and damaging winds should be the main threats, but isolated tornadoes will also be possible. Watch issuance is likely by 17Z (1 PM EDT).
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A shortwave trough over central OH and Lake Erie at 16Z will move eastward today across PA and vicinity. Isolated thunderstorms have recently initiated across central OH and northwestern PA in association with this feature. A belt of strong 50-65 kt mid-level westerly winds will be present across eastern OH, much of PA, and NJ today. Long, nearly straight hodographs through mid levels and related 40-50 kt of effective bulk shear should favor scattered splitting supercells early this afternoon. Large hail will probably be the initial concern with this convection, with some increase in the damaging wind threat with time as storms potentially congeal into one or more bowing line segments as they move east-southeastward across PA into NJ. A marine front located over the NYC metro area and adjacent northern NJ will likely limit the northeastern extent of the substantial severe threat this afternoon. In addition to the large hail and damaging wind risk, isolated tornadoes could also occur over mainly parts of central/eastern PA into portions of NJ to the east of a weak surface low where low-level southwesterly winds are forecast to be somewhat stronger. Watch issuance will likely be needed across this region by 17Z (1 PM EDT).

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for large hail, damaging winds, and a few tornadoes will continue to increase through the early afternoon. Watch issuance is likely in the next hour or two.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A very moist low-level airmass is present across north/northeast TX, southeastern OK, and southwestern/west-central AR. Surface dewpoints are generally in the low to mid 70s across this region, and a mean mixing ratio of 16.1 g/kg was noted on the 16Z special sounding from FWD. Within a low-level warm air advection regime, scattered showers and a few thunderstorms have developed across the warm sector in several pre-frontal confluence zones. Current expectations are for supercells to develop ahead of the ongoing clusters of thunderstorms in north-central TX. Given the strong instability that is already in place (MLCAPE of 2500-3000 J/kg), at least modestly steep mid-level lapse rates, and plentiful shear (effective bulk shear values of 40-50 kt), scattered large hail will be a concern. Some of the hail may be greater than 2 inches in diameter. Damaging downdraft winds will also be possible given the steepening low-level lapse rates from diurnal heating, and as convection may gradually consolidate into one or more clusters/line segments. The tornado threat across this region is a bit more uncertain, as a 25-30 kt southerly low-level jet is forecast to gradually weaken through the afternoon before restrengthening across parts of AR later this evening. Even so, an initially favorable supercell mode, and sufficient veering of winds in the low levels (with effective SRH generally around 100-200 ms/s2), should support some threat for tornadoes. New watch issuance will likely be needed in the next hour or two (by 19Z/2 PM CDT), and some of the counties in Severe Thunderstorm Watch 289 may be redefined into this new watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A segment of the QLCS moving southeast across the Ohio Valley has strengthened and may pose a severe threat. Damaging winds and large hail are possible, and a watch issuance is possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The ongoing QLCS has strengthened over northeast Kentucky as it moves southeast. This segment is moving slightly more perpendicular to the mean west/southwest flow aloft and entering a moderately buoyant/sheared environment characterized by 1500+ J/kg of MLCAPE and 40 knots of effective bulk shear. Damaging winds are the main threat, although marginally severe hail is also possible. While this segment may remain strong/severe for the next couple of hours as it moves southeast, it will eventually encounter a less conducive environment and become oriented more parallel to the mid-level westerly flow. However, given its current strength and decent cold pool development, it does pose a somewhat local/limited severe threat in the next couple of hours. A watch issuance is possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms will continue moving east/southeast across eastern West Virginia and likely to move into northern Virginia/vicinity in the next couple of hours. Some of the storms may become severe with damaging winds/large hail as the primary threats. A downstream watch remains possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An upper-level shortwave trough is moving over the Great Lakes/Ohio Valley/Mid-Atlantic today helping to spread forcing for ascent and strengthen deep layer vertical shear across the region. An ongoing QLCS stretches from eastern West Virginia back into central Kentucky. Convection has trended downward across the northeast segment of this QLCS within WW290, and the discrete storms developing ahead of the line have struggled to maintain their intensity over the last hour. Additionally, there is some concern regarding storms maintaining their structure on the lee slopes of the Appalachians. However, given the swarm/moist and moderate buoyant/sheared environment, there remains potential for storms to strengthen and new storms to develop ahead of the line. Marginally severe wind/hail are possible with the stronger storms. A downstream watch remains possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe threat should be confined to mainly southern and eastern portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 289 this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Widespread convective overturning has occurred along and north of a surface cold front that is located across central/eastern OK into far southeastern KS at 1830Z. An isolated severe hail/wind threat may persist through the afternoon across mainly southern and eastern portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 289 where a sufficient combination of instability and shear remains in place. The potential for additional convective development into central MO this afternoon remains unclear, but the environmental parameter space should be most favorable for severe thunderstorms across this area. Locations behind the front may be cleared from the watch early. ..Gleason.. 05/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A supercell has developed in western Kentucky and may be capable of severe wind/hail as it moves eastward.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Amid a warm/moist/unstable airmass, a supercell has developed along an outflow boundary in western Kentucky. This storm will likely move east/southeast along the boundary and could be capable of severe wind/hail. Given the isolated nature of the severe threat, a small severe thunderstorm watch is possible for portions of southwest/south-central Kentucky.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated large hail and damaging wind risk should develop this afternoon. Watch issuance is possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Two thunderstorms have recently developed along/ahead of a southward-moving cold front across parts of the Edwards Plateau of TX. The airmass to the south of the cold front is strongly unstable, with MLCAPE of 2000-2500 J/kg present per latest mesoanalysis estimates. A southern-stream shortwave trough embedded within a larger upper trough/low across the central Rockies and Plains is moving over far west TX this afternoon per water vapor satellite imagery. 50-60 kt of southwesterly mid-level flow will remain over this region through the afternoon and early evening, and 45-50 kt of effective bulk shear will encourage updraft organization/rotation. Isolated instances of large hail and perhaps strong/damaging winds could occur with these thunderstorms as they move eastward along/near the boundary over the next several hours. Main uncertainties include whether convective coverage will become sufficient for watch issuance, and whether storms will be undercut by the cold front and subsequently weaken. Regardless, radar trends will continue to be monitored through the afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues across portions of southwest Pennsylvania, far eastern Ohio, and far northwest West Virginia. Damaging winds and large hail remain the primary threats.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Severe thunderstorms continue to form in WW291 generally in a line oriented west-east with occasional storm development south/east of the line. As these storms move eastward, there is potential for re-development across southern/western portions of the watch into the evening. Storms will continue to move to the east/southeast through the afternoon with damaging wind gusts and large hail still as the primary severe threats. Storm modes of a QLCS with occasional discrete storms forming to the south/east will continue across the watch through the afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues across much of WW292 with damaging winds, large hail, and a few tornadoes possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An ongoing QLCS is oriented southwest to northeast across central/northeast Pennsylvania with discrete supercells developing ahead of it. The storm environment remains conducive with effective bulk shear of 40-50 knots and MLCAPE of 1500-2000+ J/kg with damaging wind gusts and large hail possible. A few tornadoes are also possible associated with supercells near the front from northeast Pennsylvania/western New Jersey. These storms should continue to move east-southeast across the region and eventually coalesce into a QLCS this evening as it reaches marine influenced, stable low-levels in eastern New Jersey.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: All severe hazards remain possible across Tornado Watch 293 in the short term.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A messy storm mode has developed across much of Tornado Watch 293 this afternoon, with numerous cells ongoing across north TX into southeastern OK and western/central AR. Strong shear and instability remain situated along/ahead of a surface cold front across this region, and all severe hazards remain possible. The large hail and isolated tornado threat should remain relatively greater across north TX and vicinity, where convection is still semi-discrete and somewhat greater low-level shear exists per recent mesoanalysis estimates. The damaging wind threat may gradually increase across parts of western/central AR if storms can grow upscale into a small bowing cluster as suggested by some convection-allowing model guidance. Finally, a small eastward extension to the Tornado Watch may be needed across north-central AR if current radar trends continue. ..Gleason.. 05/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Some increase in the large hail and damaging wind threat may occur this afternoon. Watch issuance is possible for some part of this area depending on radar trends.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Downstream of widespread convection across AR into south-central MO, more isolated thunderstorms have recently formed along a nearly stationary front draped generally east-west across central IL into western and central IN. In the wake of thunderstorms earlier today, the airmass across this area has been able to destabilize along/south of this boundary. As temperatures have warmed into the lower to mid 80s, moderate to strong instability has developed, with MLCAPE of 1500-3000 J/kg estimated from mesoanalysis. Although low-level flow remains generally weak, strong mid/upper-level winds are supporting 45-55 kt of effective bulk shear. There is some concern that an isolated large hail and strong/damaging wind threat may develop with these thunderstorms as they move generally east-northeastward. Additional convection that is developing across southern MO may also pose an isolated severe threat over the next couple of hours as it moves eastward. It remains unclear whether any portion of these regions will need a Severe Thunderstorm Watch due to nebulous large-scale forcing for ascent and related concerns about convective coverage, but radar trends will be closely monitored.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe storm or two are possible in northern Maryland this evening. A watch issuance is unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A storm recently developed over northern Maryland and an ongoing QLCS across Pennsylvania may bring severe weather into northern Maryland. Damaging winds and large hail are possible with any discrete storm given the MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/kg and effective bulk shear of 35-40 knots. Additionally, the wind threat may increase if the QLCS pushes more southeast into northern Maryland this evening. There is uncertainty regarding severe potential/coverage and given the proximity to WW292, a watch issuance is unlikely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe thunderstorms are possible this evening across portions of southern VA into northern NC. Watch is being considered for this region.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Remnant MCV is shifting east across southern WV. This feature evolved from earlier MCS over the lower OH Valley. Convection has been maintained along the leading edge of MCS cold pool which is now spreading east of the higher terrain. Over the last half hour new robust updrafts are maturing along the wind shift. With strong westerly flow aloft, it appears this activity will spread toward the southern Chesapeake and adjacent coastal regions. Damaging winds and hail are possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An additional isolated non-supercell tornado or two, associated with low-topped convection, remains possible over the next couple of hours. The brevity and short duration nature of the threat precludes a WW issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Isolated funnel clouds/brief non-supercellular tornadoes have been reported within a small area, confined to Sac and Pocahontas Counties in Iowa within the past few hours. These brief tornadoes have been generated by low-topped convective cells that are ingesting relatively high amounts of vertically-oriented surface vorticity associated with a subtle baroclinic zone, beneath a 700 mb low (providing ample lift and relatively colder temperatures aloft). Given the generally rich low-level moisture beneath the cooler temperatures/steep lapse rates aloft, ample 0-3km CAPE is in place to support vigorous low-level updrafts which will stretch the bountiful aforementioned surface vorticity to induce non-supercellular tornadogenesis. Current thinking is that an additional tornado or two remains possible until peak heating of the afternoon is past, and low-level CAPE diminishes, tempering the brief tornado threat. Given the very brief/isolated nature of the tornado threat, no WW issuance is expected.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated supercell development is possible over the next few hours. Marginally severe hail and a couple brief tornadoes are the main concerns. Given the sparse nature of the severe threat, a WW issuance is not anticipated at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Discrete convective development has recently been noted along an arcing confluence zone, where ample low-level moisture is in place, that combined with relatively steep lapse rates aloft, is contributing to modest buoyancy (1500 J/kg MLCAPE). While deep-layer and low-level shear is modest (35-40 knots effective bulk-shear and 200 m2/s2 0-3km SRH), relatively higher amounts of surface vertically oriented vorticity are present along the aforementioned baroclinic zone. As such, the kinematic environment supports the further development of discrete storms structures (perhaps the generation of supercells with the modest 0-3km SRH) which may then produce brief tornadoes through the stretching of ambient vertical vorticity via non-supercell/supercell hybrid tornado processes. In addition, the relatively steep lapse rates aloft may also support some marginally severe hail. The duration and spatial extent of the severe threat is expected to be low enough such that a WW issuance is not expected.
